question: Why is the echo not simply the original sound returning to the hearer?
premises: The echo is heard as if the sound had come back.
The same speaker does not hear the sound again in the same way distant hearers do.
People far away may fail to hear the original sound even when the echo is heard.
inference: The echo cannot be explained as the original sound traveling back to its source.
uncertainties: The compound boundaries in śabdasyāśravaṇādapi follow the transmitted reading.
plain_english: The echo is not produced by the original sound coming back, because although it is heard as if returning, the speaker does not hear it in that way and distant listeners may not hear the original sound at all.
